title: Court lets Perplexity’s AI agent shop on Amazon, overturning a ban
excerpt: A US appeals court has overturned Amazon’s injunction against Perplexity’s Comet shopping agent, ruling that an agent acting for a user is not unauthorised access.
content_html:
An AI agent can shop on Amazon whether Amazon likes it or not. A US appeals court has overturned an injunction that barred Perplexity’s shopping agent from the retailer, handing an early win to the software that browses and buys on people’s behalf.

The Ninth Circuit ruled that Amazon’s core legal claim did not hold. Because Perplexity’s Comet agent acts only when a user tells it to, the court found it is the user, not Perplexity, who is accessing Amazon’s servers.

Comet is the agent built into Perplexity’s AI browser. Point it at a product and it can navigate Amazon and complete a purchase, the kind of autonomous errand a wave of AI companies are betting will replace ordinary online shopping.

The retailer argued the agent amounted to unauthorised access, said Perplexity had disguised Comet as a normal Chrome browser to avoid detection, and pointed to a 2024 agreement in which Perplexity had agreed to pause agentic shopping.

Perplexity cast the fight as one over who controls a person’s shopping experience, arguing that users should be free to bring whatever software they like to websites they already have the right to visit.

The dispute turned on a decades-old hacking law. Amazon leaned on the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, written for a very different kind of intrusion, and the court decided that a tool doing a user’s bidding does not fit its definition of unauthorised access.

The reasoning is the real prize. If an agent acting on a user’s instruction is legally the user, then platforms lose one of their sharpest tools for keeping third-party agents out, and the door to agentic commerce swings open.

For Amazon, that is precisely the fear. It has spent years designing a shopping experience it controls, from search ranking to recommendations, and an agent that skips all of it strips the retailer of the influence, and the ad revenue, that layer generates.

Amazon has been building its own agentic layer, putting Alexa inside the search bar as it races to own the shopping agent rather than be bypassed by someone else’s.

The shift is already well underway elsewhere. China’s biggest platforms have gone furthest, replacing the search bar with AI agents that shop for users, a preview of where Western retail may be heading.

The mechanics are converging too. Alibaba has wired its own model straight into Taobao for end-to-end agentic shopping, the sort of first-party integration Amazon would prefer to a rival’s bot crawling its aisles.

The fight is not over. Amazon said it remains confident and is weighing its options, which include seeking a rehearing or asking the Supreme Court, while the underlying lawsuit continues in a San Francisco court.

But an appeals-court ruling carries weight. It gives other agent-makers a template to argue that acting for a user is not hacking, and it puts platforms on notice that blanket bans may not survive contact with the law.

It also nudges a bigger, unsettled question. When an agent does something harmful rather than helpful, it is still unclear who is liable, and treating the agent as the user has consequences well beyond a shopping cart.

The stakes are commercial as much as legal. Retail media has become one of Amazon’s fastest-growing profit lines, and an agent that ignores sponsored placements and buys the cheapest match threatens the ad economics holding much of that business together.

The deeper tension is structural. Websites were built for humans clicking through pages, and a bot that reads and buys at machine speed strains both the technical assumptions and the business models underneath them.

For now, the agents have the upper hand. A court blocked the web’s biggest retailer from keeping them out, in a ruling that may prove much bigger than it first appears.

content_html_zh:
无论亚马逊喜欢与否，人工智能代理都可以在亚马逊上购物。 美国一家上诉法院推翻了一项禁止 Perplexity 的购物代理进入零售商的禁令，让这款代表人们浏览和购买的软件赢得了先机。

第九巡回法院裁定亚马逊的核心法律主张不成立。 由于 Perplexity 的 Comet 代理仅在用户指示时才起作用，因此法院认为访问亚马逊服务器的是用户，而不是 Perplexity。

Comet 是 Perplexity 人工智能浏览器中内置的代理。 将其对准产品，它就可以在亚马逊上导航并完成购买，一波人工智能公司押注这种自主任务将取代普通的在线购物。

该零售商辩称，该代理相当于未经授权的访问，并表示 Perplexity 将 Comet 伪装成普通的 Chrome 浏览器以避免检测，并指出了 2024 年的一份协议，其中 Perplexity 同意暂停代理购物。

《困惑》将这场斗争归结为谁控制一个人的购物体验，认为用户应该可以自由地将他们喜欢的任何软件带到他们已经有权访问的网站上。

这场争端的起因是一项已有数十年历史的黑客法。 亚马逊依靠的是《计算机欺诈和滥用法案》，该法案是针对一种非常不同类型的入侵而制定的，法院裁定，执行用户命令的工具不符合其对未经授权访问的定义。

推理才是真正的奖品。 如果按照用户指令行事的代理人在法律上就是用户，那么平台就会失去将第三方代理人拒之门外的最锋利的工具之一，代理商业的大门就会敞开。

对于亚马逊来说，这正是恐惧所在。 它花了数年时间设计自己控制的购物体验，从搜索排名到推荐，而跳过所有这些的代理会剥夺零售商的影​​响力和该层产生的广告收入。

亚马逊一直在构建自己的代理层，将 Alexa 放在搜索栏中，因为它竞相拥有购物代理，而不是被其他人绕过。

这种转变已经在其他地方顺利进行。 中国最大的平台走得最远，用为用户购物的人工智能代理取代了搜索栏，这是西方零售业可能走向的预览。

机制也在趋同。 阿里巴巴已将自己的模式直接接入淘宝，进行端到端代理购物，亚马逊更喜欢这种第一方集成，而不是竞争对手的机器人在其过道上爬行。

战斗还没有结束。 亚马逊表示，它仍然充满信心，并正在权衡各种选择，其中包括寻求重审或向最高法院提出请求，而基本诉讼仍在旧金山法院继续进行。

但上诉法院的裁决具有重要意义。 它为其他代理制造商提供了一个模板，可以证明为用户代理不是黑客行为，并且它让平台注意到，一旦触犯法律，全面禁令可能无法继续存在。

它还触动了一个更大的、悬而未决的问题。 当代理人做了有害而不是有益的事情时，仍然不清楚谁应该承担责任，并且将代理人视为用户所产生的后果远远超出了购物车的范围。

这些股份既是商业性的，也是合法的。 零售媒体已经成为亚马逊增长最快的利润线之一，而忽视赞助广告并购买最便宜的比赛的代理商会威胁到维持大部分业务的广告经济。

更深层次的紧张是结构性的。 网站是为人类点击页面而构建的，而以机器速度阅读和购买的机器人对技术假设和其背后的商业模式都造成了压力。

目前来看，代理商占据上风。 一家法院阻止了网络上最大的零售商将他们排除在外，这一裁决可能比最初看起来要大得多。
